Thanks for the time today, Tom — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the benchmark run: 

1) Your stated SLO targets (confirm below):
- p95 latency <= 150ms for 512-token responses
- sustained throughput ~500 req/s
- concurrent sessions: 200 active connections
- streaming required (token-by-token delivery, ~10 tokens/sec on average)

2) What we need from your side to start an official benchmark:
- canonical prompt set (happy to accept JSON or CSV)
- examples of streaming expectations (client-side playback/SDK)
- representative input distribution (short/long requests mix)

3) What we'll provide:
- benchmark harness (Docker + runbook) and measurement definitions (p50/p95/p99, tail latency, cold vs warm)
- reproducibility notes and hardware spec used for runs
- summary report and follow-up calibration plan

Attachments: I’ve attached a template prompt set and our standard benchmark harness doc to this thread (edgefin-benchmark-prompts-v1.json; redwood-benchmark-harness.md).

Proposed next steps: if you can confirm the SLO numbers above and drop your canonical prompt set, Dev will schedule a preliminary run next week. If the targets are accurate, we’ll also provide an estimated wall time for the full throughput/concurrency run.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming our targets and adding clarifications: 

- p95 <= 150ms for responses up to 512 tokens (we care most about p95; p99 target is 250ms).
- Throughput: baseline 500 req/s, peak bursts up to 900 req/s for ~2 minute windows.
- Concurrency: 200 long-lived streaming sessions (mostly single-stream streams, not multiplexed).
- Streaming: token-by-token; client expects first token within 50-70ms and steady token cadence ~10-12 tokens/sec.

I’m attaching our canonical prompt set (edgefin-benchmark-prompts-v1.json). It includes a mix: 60% short prompts (<50 tokens), 30% medium (50-200), 10% long (>200).

Questions for your team:
- Will the harness simulate our burst traffic pattern and long-lived streaming sessions?
- Can you isolate p95 for streaming-first-token separately from overall response p95?

Tom

Hi Tom — thanks, this is very helpful. A few notes on the benchmark methodology and what we’ll measure so expectations are aligned: 

1) Harness & reproducibility
- We’ll run the Redwood benchmark harness (attached: redwood-benchmark-harness.md) inside an isolated network namespace. The harness is deterministic given the same prompt set and RNG seed.
- We provide a Docker image and a runbook. For reproducibility, we’ll share the run script, seed, and the exact model binary/quantization profile used.

2) Measurement definitions
- p95/p99/median: measured on end-to-end request completion time (for non-streaming).
- streaming-first-token latency: time between request start and first byte delivered to client. We’ll report streaming-first-token p50/p95/p99 independently.
- token throughput: tokens/sec aggregated over the run windows (we’ll report sustained and burst windows).
- concurrency semantics: we simulate long-lived streaming connections (200 concurrent) by maintaining open HTTP/2 streams and sending new request payloads per your mix.

3) Warmup & run strategy
- Warmup: we’ll do a 10-minute warmup at ~60% of target throughput to populate KV cache and JIT kernels.
- Full run: three iterations: baseline (500 req/s sustained for 15 minutes), burst patterns (simulate 900 req/s bursts with 2-minute windows repeated 3x), and concurrency-driven test (200 streaming sessions sustained for 20 minutes).
- Each run will include telemetry: per-request timing, network RTT, server CPU/GPU utilization, and token emission traces for streaming tests.

4) Environment & hardware
- We’ll run initial tests on our Dedicated cluster using 8xA100-80GB (NVIDIA A100) instances; we’ll note exact driver/kernel/kubelet versions in the report. If you prefer a different SKU, tell us.
- We’ll include quantization/profile info (FP16 vs int8-quant) and any kernel-level optimizations used.

5) Artifacts we’ll share
- Raw logs + aggregated CSV (sample: sample-results-run1.csv), per-run runbook, and a reproducibility guide with exact commands and Docker image SHA.

Answering your questions: Yes — the harness can simulate your burst pattern and will maintain long-lived streams. We will report streaming-first-token latency separately from overall response latency.

Proposed next step: if you’re good with the methodology, Marissa and I can schedule the first run next Tuesday (2026-02-24). Expect ~4-6 hours of wall time for the full set of iterations (including warmups and data collection); we’ll provide an interim summary after the baseline run (~1 hour).

Attaching: redwood-benchmark-harness.md (runbook + docker image refs)

Regards,
